newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX sets new records but nerves set in.
newsitem.headline: German DAX sets new records but nerves set in.

text.p: The persistently firm dollar and Wall Street's rally kept German shares on their record-breaking trail in Friday's bourse trade, although nerves set in as the session continued.

The 30-share blue chip DAX index ended the floor session up 18.70 points at a new record close of 3,248.18 points, catching up with a sharp advance in late screen-based trade Thursday, but slipped some 20 points off its intraday high of 3,271.91.
"We are clearly totally dependent on the dollar," said one dealer. "How we proceed in the share market hinges completely on whether the dollar holds."

The dollar, holding its own despite the Bundesbank's verbal attempts earlier this week to slow its gains, was trading just below 1.69 marks during the German share trade session, although key economic data from the U.S. in the afternoon was expected to affect the currency.

Some dealers also said the DAX looked vulnerable to a correction as it teetered at heights virtually unimaginable only weeks ago. The index has gained two percent this week and 14 percent since the start of January.
"You get the feeling a lot of the funds are already fully invested," said one dealer.

Bank stocks were in the spotlight, generally posting gains, after Morgan Stanley upgraded its outlook for their stocks while Moody's Investor Service said it had placed Dresdner Bank's AAA credit rating under review.
Shrugging off the news, Dresdner shares climbed 50 pfennigs to 53.90 marks, as it said it did not expect any refinancing problems even if Moody's went ahead with the downgrade.

Metallgesellschaft rose 1.32 marks to 34.15 marks after Thursday's late news that it had decided not to take on a 49.99 percent stake in industrial holding company AGIV -- a move which the market feared would have diluted its profits.

However utility Viag declined six marks to 703 after posting a rise in 1996 profit that was broadly in line with expectations, but prompted some shift of interest to rivals in the sector whose earnings position is still unclear.
